title: Calculate Average Order Value (AOV)
description: Average Order Value is total revenue divided by the number of DISTINCT orders (not the number of line items - one order usually has several). Write a query that returns the AOV, rounded to 2 decimal places, as `average_order_value`.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: COUNT(DISTINCT ...), ROUND

order_items has one row PER PRODUCT in an order, so COUNT(*) would overcount orders that bought multiple products - COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) counts each order exactly once no matter how many line items it has.
ROUND(SUM(quantity * unit_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), 2), aliased as average_order_value, from order_items.
expected_behavior: Returns one row, one column (average_order_value): total revenue divided by the number of distinct orders, rounded to 2 decimals.
solution: SELECT ROUND(SUM(quantity * unit_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), 2) AS average_order_value FROM order_items;
explanation: COUNT(DISTINCT column) is the key idea here - without DISTINCT, an order with 3 line items would be counted 3 times, silently deflating the average.
